text:
sara (Docs): heads-up — i'm opening a small PR to clarify the optimize toolkit page on batching vs kv-prefetch. noticed a couple broken links and an ambiguous example for short sequences.
kevin (Eng): nice, can you paste the snippet you're planning to swap?
sara (Docs): sure — current python snippet in docs uses our old client call: 
```python
client.generate(model='redwood-v1', prompt=p, max_tokens=64)
```
it doesn't show batch-friendly usage or kv-prefetch options. i want to replace with a short example showing batch_send + prefetch hint.
tomas (ML): please also call out the quant profile caveat for models that don't support fp16 kv cache — i've seen regressions when people combine aggressive quant + prefetch.
li (DevEx): +1. can we include both go and py snippets? a few customers asked for go examples last week.
sara (Docs): yep — i'll add a tiny go example and annotate where to enable prefetch. e.g. 
```go
reqs := []GenerateRequest{...}
client.BatchGenerate(ctx, reqs, WithKVPrefetch(true))
```
kevin (Eng): API note: the go helper is called BatchGenerate(ctx, requests, opts...). there's also a helper for PrefixCache. mention that the runtime will ignore prefetch for extremely short prefixes (<8 tokens) to avoid overhead.
sara (Docs): good call — i'll add a parenthetical about the short-prefix threshold. also found 2 broken internal links: one points to an old optkit PR, the other to an example that moved. will fix.
docbot: automated reminder: link-check CI will run on pr #5247 once opened.
maya (QA): can you add a tiny test case in the examples repo that demonstrates batching latency improvement? i can run perf locally on my machine.
sara (Docs): yes — plan: docs PR + examples change + perf smoke. PRs: docs -> #5247, examples -> #5248. i'll request review from kevin and tomas.
kevin (Eng): ACK. i'll look at API wording. if you mention kv-prefetch, add a short note about memory tradeoffs and the prefetch window param.
tomas (ML): for quant profiles, add a recommendation: "avoid 4-bit quantization for llama-family when prefix caching is critical; test with a pinned eval set" — link to internal eval guide.
li (DevEx): also add a small troubleshooting note for SDK streaming + batching interaction — that bit is easy to miss.
sara (Docs): will do. question: is there a preferred place in the doc tree for the go snippet? under "code samples" or inline in the batching section?
kevin (Eng): inline makes the most sense for context, and include a link to a dedicated code-samples page for longer examples.
sara (Docs): thanks. i'll open the PR later today; will tag @kevin and @tomas and assign to li for snippet style check.
docbot: CI queued: docs/lint, link-checker, examples/smoke (expected run in ~10m).
kevin (Eng): quick nit — please avoid the word "aggressive" without numbers. prefer explicit thresholds (e.g., prefetch_window=32).
sara (Docs): noted. i'll add explicit numbers and a short table with recommended defaults for small/medium/large workloads.
maya (QA): once PRs are up, assign to me for the perf runs (i'll provide numbers for the changelog entry).
sara (Docs): perfect — thanks everyone :tada:
li (DevEx): ping if you want me to do a short sample-format pass after the PR lands.
sara (Docs): will do. final checklist in PR description: 1) fix broken links 2) add py+go snippets 3) call out short-prefix threshold and memory tradeoffs 4) add quant-profile recommendation and eval link 5) examples change + perf smoke 6) request reviews from kevin/tomas/li/maya.
kevin (Eng): sounds good. thanks for pulling this together.
